issues.title: fork setup and licensing
issues.description: Stand up the fork-based in-tree strategy from BRIEF.md: vorssaint-utils vendored as our engine layer, our targets added alongside, GPLv3 in place from the first commit. Nothing else can start until the package builds.

issues.title: activate/deactivate lifecycle and idle CPU
issues.description: Sampling runs only while the panel is visible, except for widgets that explicitly opt into background sampling for a menu-bar stat. Enforced through activate()/deactivate(). Engine work off the main thread, models publish on main.

issues.title: edit mode: wiggle, remove, and drag between lanes
issues.description: Long-press or an Edit button enters edit mode. Widgets wiggle via a small repeating rotationEffect with a random per-item phase offset so they do not sync, show remove badges, and become draggable. Prefer a custom drag gesture plus matchedGeometryEffect over .draggable/.dropDestination, which feel clunky for grid reordering. Drop targets: any position in any lane, plus an empty trailing lane that appears as a target to create a new lane.

issues.title: lane layout with placeholder widgets
issues.description: Vertical lanes stacking widget cards, driven by the layout model and rendering whatever the registry provides. Placeholder widgets only at this stage.

issues.title: glass card design system
issues.description: The CCPUI vocabulary every widget draws from: spacing scale, corner radii (continuous, ~16-20), thin-material card fill, 1px white-alpha stroke, shadow, type ramp, accent for active toggles. Matches macOS Control Center's language; borrows nothing from Vorssaint, whose design is trademarked.

issues.title: panel dismissal and multi-display behaviour
issues.description: Dismiss on outside click via a global NSEvent monitor, and on Esc. Show on the display holding the status item (or the mouse). The event monitor must be removed when the panel closes — a leaked global monitor is the classic version of this bug.

issues.title: status item and non-activating glass panel
issues.description: NSStatusItem toggles an NSPanel: .nonactivatingPanel, level .popUpMenu, collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary]. Real blur via NSVisualEffectView (.hudWindow or .popover, blendingMode .behindWindow) wrapped for SwiftUI. Anchored top-right of the screen holding the status item, width growing leftward with lane count up to full width. Pre-warm the window at launch.

issues.title: layout model and persistence
issues.description: [Lane] where Lane = [WidgetID], Codable, persisted as JSON in Application Support. Decoding must survive a stored layout naming a widget the registry no longer has, without discarding the rest of the arrangement.

issues.title: design the CCPWidget protocol and registry
issues.description: Everything hangs off this, so it comes first. CCPWidget with a static WidgetDescriptor (id, title, icon, default size, required permissions), makeView(), activate()/deactivate(), optional settings and compact/expanded variants. Plus WidgetRegistry listing what is available.

issues.title: the shell: panel, lanes, edit mode
issues.description: The glass panel and everything structural around widgets, built with placeholder widgets only. Per BRIEF: get the shell feeling great before wiring any engine.

issues.title: migrate the MEMORY.md dashboard note into bd remember
issues.description:
The shared-memory rule now ships in AGENTS.md: bd remember is the durable cross-tool memory because every agent here has bd and the brief already prints the keys, while a tool's own memory stays native and holds pointers.

This repo's memory directory still has the fact rather than the pointer. ~/.claude/projects/-Users-bubbles-dev-control-center-pro/memory/ holds a note that the dashboard opens in Claude Code's browser pane and never the system browser, on port 7393. That is a project fact every session needs and it is invisible to opencode, Codex, and anything else that isn't Claude Code — the exact failure the rule exists to prevent, sitting in the file that documents the rule.
issues.design: bd remember it, leave a one-line pointer in MEMORY.md. Per .claude/HARNESS.md, anything removed from the memory directory is copied to .claude/memory-archive/ and shown to the user first — this is a rewrite rather than a removal, but the archive copy is cheap insurance on the one edit in this project that has no git revert behind it.

issues.title: bd makes its own git commits, and they bypass the commit-msg hook
issues.description:
Running 'bd dolt remote add' produced commit 815bc9b 'bd: update sync.remote' — authored as the user, not requested, touching .beads/config.yaml (it stripped the trailing newline, nothing more).

Two problems:
1. bd commits to git on its own. This repo's profile is conservative about git actions, and CLAUDE.md says not to commit without authority. A tool that commits as a side effect of a config read/write breaks that expectation silently.
2. The message names no bead. scripts/hooks/commit-msg would reject 'bd: update sync.remote' — the regex needs a ccp- id — so bd is committing with the hook bypassed. That is the same drift ccp-jze was filed for, except the bypass is not a human typing --no-verify, it is a tool doing it invisibly.

Nothing was harmed here; the commit is a one-character whitespace change. The concern is the mechanism.
issues.notes: Found while wiring the Dolt transport (ccp-0t2). Same class of issue as ccp-jze, which removed the --no-verify advertisement from the hook.

issues.title: workflow skill staleness gate is blind — context.py picks first tracks comment
issues.description: scripts/context.py:50 uses re.search for '<!-- tracks:' which finds the example comment at .claude/skills/workflow/SKILL.md:108 ('<!-- tracks: … -->') instead of the real tracks at :196. So lock entry is {'…': ''} and none of the 5 real sources (brief.sh, verify.sh, dashboard.py, hooks/commit-msg, context.py) are actually watched — e.g. editing scripts/hooks/commit-msg for ccp-jze did not trigger STALE as it should. Same risk for any doc that mentions tracks: in prose. Fix: make tracked_by find the *last* tracks comment, or anchor to end-of-file, and bless afterwards.

issues.title: CCP's own app bundle still inherits upstream's Vorssaint build identity (build.sh EXECUTABLE=Vorssaint, APP_BUNDLE_ID=com.vorssaint.utils)

issues.title: README build instructions advertise a build that produces a Vorssaint bundle
issues.description: README.md:71-78 tells people to run ./build.sh and ./build.sh --install, but build.sh is upstream tooling that sets EXECUTABLE=Vorssaint and APP_BUNDLE_ID=com.vorssaint.utils (build.sh:27-36). The same README states CCP 'presents no modified build as Vorssaint', and TRADEMARKS.md requires forks to use a different name, icon and bundle identifier. So the README instructs the reader to do the exact thing the README and TRADEMARKS.md forbid. The underlying identity fix is ccp-v64; this bead is the README not advertising it in the meantime.
issues.close_reason: README's build section now uses 'swift build' and states plainly that build.sh still emits a com.vorssaint.utils bundle TRADEMARKS.md forbids a fork from shipping, pointing at ccp-v64 for the rename. Placeholder clone URL replaced with the real origin. Committed 3d28645.

issues.title: README links upstream's docs as CCP's — security reports misroute to Vorssaint
issues.description: The README rewrite (e9cddfb) presents SUPPORT.md, SECURITY.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and CHANGELOG.md as CCP's docs, but all four are still upstream's, untouched by the fork. SECURITY.md sends vulnerability reports to vorssaintapp/vorssaint-utils/security/advisories/new, so a CCP security report lands in the upstream maintainer's private advisories. SUPPORT.md points bug reports at upstream's issue tracker. CONTRIBUTING.md is titled 'Contributing to Vorssaint' and describes upstream's layout, yet README cites it twice as covering CCP's layout and conventions. CHANGELOG.md is entirely Vorssaint releases with no CCP entries.
issues.design: Rewrite SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's (real consequence, and conflicts on upstream merge are rare and cheap). Do NOT overwrite CONTRIBUTING.md or CHANGELOG.md — they are upstream files that keep receiving upstream commits, and overwriting them makes 'merge upstream/main' expensive, which the fork strategy depends on staying cheap. Relabel those two in the README as upstream's instead.
issues.close_reason: Rewrote SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md as CCP's own; security advisories now route to bubblesunyum/control-center-pro with an explicit split for vendored upstream sources. README no longer presents CONTRIBUTING.md/CHANGELOG.md as CCP's — labelled as vendored upstream rather than forked, to keep 'merge upstream/main' cheap. Reviewed by reviewer-taste and reviewer-correctness (both clean, all links and claims verified against the repo); scripts/verify.sh passed. Committed 3d28645.

issues.title: commits bypassed the commit-msg hook with --no-verify
issues.description: 3f01781, 6001d7f and ffb9bbc were all committed after 2897fe7 installed a working blocking commit-msg hook, and none names a bead — only --no-verify gets past it. Nothing to backfill without rewriting history. The open question is whether the hook should stop advertising 'git commit --no-verify' in its own refusal text, since that is the line that gets taken. Consider requiring a reason, or logging bypasses so the drift is at least visible.
issues.close_reason: removed the 'Genuinely unfilable? git commit --no-verify' hint from scripts/hooks/commit-msg:39-41 per option #1. Hook now only directs to bd q / bd ready and the required bead id. Verified: blocks missing bead without advertising bypass, passes with ccp-jze, passes fixup!, and scripts/verify.sh passes.

skills.name: agentic-review
skills.description: Review a control-center-pro change with agents that didn't write it — taste against the project's standards, correctness hunting real defects, and design reading screenshots of what actually rendered. Use before committing a non-trivial change, when asked to review work or a branch, or after finishing a feature.

skills.name: beads
skills.description: Use when working in a repository that uses bd or Beads for durable project task tracking, issue dependencies, blocker management, multi-session handoff, or shared work memory. Trigger when the user asks to find ready work, claim or close tasks, create follow-up work, inspect blockers, recover project context, or choose between local planning and persistent project tracking.

skills.name: handoff
skills.description: Close out a control-center-pro session on purpose — settle the ledger, leave a note for whoever wakes up next, and optionally hand straight off to a fresh agent. Use when work is wrapping up, when the context window is getting long, or when the user says to hand off, wrap up, or take a beat.

skills.name: workflow
skills.description: How work moves through control-center-pro — the beads ledger, the verify gate, the review pass, and the token budget that keeps them affordable on one account. Use when starting a work session, deciding where a note or a discovery belongs, planning a multi-step change, handing off at the end of a session, or wondering which skill or script to reach for.

agents.name: librarian
agents.description: Audits the whole knowledge layer at once — every skill, every memory, and what a session pays before it starts — and proposes what to merge, delete, shorten, or promote. Reads a digest rather than the repo. Run on a cadence or when the always-loaded cost climbs, never on the hot path of doing work.

agents.name: reviewer-correctness
agents.description: Hunts for real defects in a control-center-pro diff — logic errors, concurrency bugs, lifecycle and state mistakes, and the platform traps this project keeps hitting. Reads a review packet and reports only findings with a concrete failure scenario.

agents.name: reviewer-design
agents.description: Reviews screenshots of a control-center-pro change — what the app actually renders, not what the diff says it should. Hunts clipping, truncation, overflow, misalignment, and drift from the app's established look. Reads a review packet listing captures to look at. Use whenever a change touches anything on screen.

agents.name: reviewer-taste
agents.description: Reviews a control-center-pro diff against the project's documented taste — composition, module size, naming, comments, accessibility. Covers the app and the harness scripts. Reads a review packet and reports violations. Runs on a cheap model; use for every change worth reviewing.

nodes.name: agentic-review
nodes.role: Review a control-center-pro change with agents that didn't write it — taste against the project's standards, correctness hunting real defects, and design reading screenshots of what actually rendered. Use before committing a non-trivial change, when asked to review work or a branch, or after finishing a feature.

nodes.name: handoff
nodes.role: Close out a control-center-pro session on purpose — settle the ledger, leave a note for whoever wakes up next, and optionally hand straight off to a fresh agent. Use when work is wrapping up, when the context window is getting long, or when the user says to hand off, wrap up, or take a beat.

harness.name: prove
harness.blurb: the gate a change passes before it counts

nodes.name: verify.sh
nodes.role: build, tests, and a smoke check, one exit code

harness.name: review
harness.blurb: agents that didn't write the code reading it

nodes.name: review.sh
nodes.role: bundles the diff into one packet

nodes.name: librarian
nodes.role: Audits the whole knowledge layer at once — every skill, every memory, and what a session pays before it starts — and proposes what to merge, delete, shorten, or promote. Reads a digest rather than the repo. Run on a cadence or when the always-loaded cost climbs, never on the hot path of doing work.

nodes.name: reviewer-correctness
nodes.role: Hunts for real defects in a control-center-pro diff — logic errors, concurrency bugs, lifecycle and state mistakes, and the platform traps this project keeps hitting. Reads a review packet and reports only findings with a concrete failure scenario.

nodes.name: reviewer-design
nodes.role: Reviews screenshots of a control-center-pro change — what the app actually renders, not what the diff says it should. Hunts clipping, truncation, overflow, misalignment, and drift from the app's established look. Reads a review packet listing captures to look at. Use whenever a change touches anything on screen.

nodes.name: reviewer-taste
nodes.role: Reviews a control-center-pro diff against the project's documented taste — composition, module size, naming, comments, accessibility. Covers the app and the harness scripts. Reads a review packet and reports violations. Runs on a cheap model; use for every change worth reviewing.

harness.name: tend
harness.blurb: keeping the knowledge layer true and small

nodes.name: context.py
nodes.role: stale-doc and context-budget guard

nodes.name: context.lock
nodes.role: hashes of what each doc describes
